components.note: Standard annotated edition.

components.title: Paradise Lost — Doré edition
components.note: Doré's defining illustration set.

components.title: The Poetical Works of John Milton

megabooks.title: The Arabian Nights
megabooks.author: Various
megabooks.description: Three complete English editions of the Thousand and One Nights, spanning 1910–1924.

megabooks.title: Leaves of Grass
megabooks.author: Walt Whitman
megabooks.description: Walt Whitman's defining collection in three editions — 1897, 1900, and the 1921 posthumous edition.

megabooks.title: Acâibü'l-Mahlûkât · The Book of Wonders
megabooks.author: Zakarīyā ibn Muḥammad al-Qazwīnī
megabooks.description: The 13th-century Islamic cosmography — Ottoman, Persian, and French editions spanning 1553–1866, with AI-translated English layer.

components.title: Book of Wonders (Ottoman, 1553)
components.note: Ottoman Turkish manuscript.

components.title: Book of Wonders (Persian, 1565)
components.note: Persian manuscript — 176 pages, in progress.

components.title: ʻAjāʾib al-makhlūqāt — Persian text (AI transcription)
components.contributor: Transcribed from the 1565 manuscript by Claude (AI)
components.note: A complete AI transcription of the manuscript into readable Persian text, all 713 pages, beside the original scans — unverified, offered so readers can check it against the source.

components.title: The Wonders of Creation — English (AI translation from the Persian)
components.contributor: Translated from the Persian by Claude (AI)
components.note: The first known English rendering of this Persian manuscript, all 713 pages — a distinct textual witness from the Ottoman translation elsewhere in this megabook, worth comparing. Generated by AI directly from the manuscript, unverified, with the source scan one tap away on every page.

megabooks.title: Ancient & Classical Herbalism
megabooks.author: Various
megabooks.description: The foundational plant medicine texts of the ancient world — Egyptian, Greek, Ayurvedic, Chinese, and Mesoamerican primary sources.

components.title: Papyrus Ebers (c.1550 BCE)
components.note: Oldest surviving medical document. 700 remedies across 110 pages of hieratic script.

components.title: De Materia Medica — Dioscorides
components.note: 600 plants documented by the Greek physician who served Nero's army. The foundational pharmacopoeia for 1,500 years.

components.title: Charaka Samhita (c.600 BCE)
components.note: Core Ayurvedic compendium. Documents 340 plant drugs across 8 branches of medicine.

components.title: Bencao Gangmu (本草綱目, 1596)
components.note: The Great Pharmacopoeia. 1,892 medicinal substances documented over 27 years — the largest premodern natural history in any language.

components.title: Shennong Bencao Jing (c.200 CE)
components.note: The Divine Farmer's Classic — 365 plant, mineral, and animal drugs in three grades.

components.title: Badianus Manuscript (1552)
components.contributor: Martín de la Cruz / Juan Badianus
components.note: First New World herbal. Aztec physician documents 180 Nahuatl plant remedies with color illustrations — unique surviving copy.

components.title: Historia del Nuevo Mundo (1653)
components.note: Jesuit natural history of the Americas. Documents medicinal uses of hundreds of plants across Andean and Mesoamerican traditions.

megabooks.title: Asian Botanical Medicine
megabooks.author: Various
megabooks.description: Traditional medical texts from Korea, Japan, Tibet, Persia, and the Islamic world.

components.title: Dongui Bogam (東醫寶鑑, 1613)
components.note: UNESCO Memory of the World. Korea's National Treasure No.1085. 25 volumes synthesizing 2,000 years of East Asian medicine.

components.title: Dongui Bogam — Original Manuscript (NLK scans)
components.note: All 25 volumes as manuscript facsimile scans from the National Library of Korea.

components.title: Gyushi — Four Tantras of Tibetan Medicine
components.note: The foundational text of Tibetan medicine. 156 chapters across four tantras.

components.title: The Canon of Medicine (1025)
components.note: The most influential medical textbook in history. Used in European universities until the 17th century. 800+ plant drugs.

components.title: Kampo Traditional Medicine
components.note: Japanese adaptation of Chinese medicine — 210 classical formulas still used in modern Japanese healthcare.

components.title: Yamato Honzo (大和本草, 1709)
components.note: Foundational encyclopedia of Japanese natural history. 1,362 plant species — first systematic separation of Japanese from Chinese botany.

components.title: Honzo Wamyo (本草和名, 918 CE)
components.note: Japan's oldest surviving pharmacopoeia. Japanese vernacular names alongside Chinese pharmaceutical terms.

components.title: Avestan / Zoroastrian Plant Medicine
components.note: Plant medicine from the Zoroastrian tradition — haoma, medicinal herbs of ancient Persia.

megabooks.title: African Plant Medicine
megabooks.author: Various
megabooks.description: Traditional plant medicine from across the African continent — West African, East African, South African, and Ethiopian traditions.

components.title: West African Traditional Medicine
components.note: Plant knowledge of the Guinea Coast and Sahel — 648 passages documenting medicinal plants across the healing traditions of West Africa.

components.title: Southern African Traditional Medicine
components.note: Plant medicine of the San, Zulu, Xhosa, and Khoikhoi — including Aloe ferox, Buchu, Rooibos, and Hoodia.

components.title: Ethiopian & East African Medicine
components.note: Plant medicine of Ethiopia, Kenya, and East Africa including Kigelia africana and Hagenia abyssinica.

megabooks.title: Plant Medicine of the Americas
megabooks.author: Various
megabooks.description: Indigenous and traditional plant medicine from North America, the Amazon, Mesoamerica, and the Philippines.

components.title: North American Indigenous Medicine
components.note: Plant knowledge of Native American nations — Echinacea, Black cohosh, Goldenseal, Sassafras, and 60+ other medicinal plants.

components.title: Amazonian Plant Medicine
components.note: Plant medicine of the Amazon basin — Ayahuasca (Banisteriopsis caapi), Cat's claw, Sangre de drago, and 16 other compounds.

components.title: Maya Botanical Medicine
components.note: Plant remedies from the Maya tradition documented in colonial-era texts and surviving codices.

components.title: Philippine Traditional Medicine
components.note: Plant medicine of the Philippine archipelago — Betel, Lagundi, Akapulko, Sambong.

components.title: Australian Aboriginal Plant Medicine
components.note: Plant knowledge of Australian Aboriginal peoples — Tea tree, Eucalyptus, Kangaroo apple, and 15 more.

megabooks.title: European Botanical Medicine
megabooks.author: Various
megabooks.description: Medieval, Celtic, Anglo-Saxon, Italian Renaissance, Russian, Welsh, Norse, and modern European botanical medicine texts — including manuscript facsimiles.

components.title: Bald's Leechbook — Manuscript (c.950 CE)
components.note: England's oldest medical compendium. British Library Royal MS 12 D XVII. 279 pages. A remedy in this book was recently proven to kill MRSA.

components.title: Leechdoms, Wortcunning & Starcraft (1864)
components.note: 546 pages. Cockayne's bilingual edition — Old English original beside English translation. Contains Bald's Leechbook, Old English Herbarium, and the Lacnunga charm collection.

components.title: Erbario — Italian Herbal Manuscript (c.1400)
components.note: 180 botanical illustrations. Human-faced mandrake roots prescribed as anesthetics. The bridge between medieval and Renaissance botanical science.

components.title: Matthioli — Di Pedacio Dioscoride (1544)
components.note: 448 pages. First Italian vernacular translation of Dioscorides. The most influential herbal of the Renaissance. English translation in progress.

components.title: Meddygon Myddfai (c.1300)
components.note: Oldest surviving Welsh herbal. Hereditary physicians of Myddfai blend Celtic, Druidic, and Christian healing traditions — 30 plant entries documented.

components.title: Norse & Scandinavian Plant Medicine
components.note: Nine Herb Charm (invokes Odin, c.1000 CE), Henrik Harpestraeng Liber Herbarum (c.1244), and Icelandic manuscripts.

components.title: Russian Travnik — Monastery Herbal Tradition
components.note: Russian Orthodox monastery herbal medicine. Byzantine learning, Central Asian influence, and Siberian plant knowledge — Chaga, Rhodiola, Sea buckthorn.

components.title: German Commission E Monographs
components.contributor: German Federal Institute for Drugs and Medical Devices
components.note: 126 evidence-based plant monographs — the gold standard of phytomedicine regulatory review.

components.title: American Herbal Pharmacopoeia
components.note: 45 full-quality plant monographs with clinical evidence review.

components.title: WHO Monographs on Selected Medicinal Plants
components.note: 94 validated plant monographs — the authoritative global standard for plant medicine.

megabooks.title: Caribbean Travellers
megabooks.author: Various
megabooks.description: First-person accounts of the Caribbean from the 1820s to the 1890s — captains' logs, colonial administrators' diaries, and naturalists' observations, with extensive firsthand documentation of Anguilla.

components.title: Six Months in the West Indies in 1825
components.note: The richest single account of 1820s Anguilla — a full dedicated chapter.

components.title: Down the Islands: A Voyage to the Caribbees
components.note: Full chapter on Anguilla, Irish settlers, and a 200-year-old French spy's report.

components.title: Gossip of the Caribbees
components.note: Literary account of a colonial administrator's isolated posting to Anguilla — visited monthly by a mail ship.

components.title: Trinidad and the Other West India Islands and Colonies
components.note: Includes dedicated Anguilla section: 1746 French attack repelled, revenue figures, governance.

components.title: The West Indies
components.note: Entire chapter (XX) on Anguilla, St. Martin, Barbuda. Opens with the island's 'snake' name etymology.

megabooks.title: Caribbean History — Primary Documents
megabooks.author: Various
megabooks.description: Official documents, legal records, and firsthand historical accounts of the Caribbean from the 1830s to the early 20th century.

components.title: Emancipation in the West Indies
components.contributor: James A. Thome & J. Horace Kimball
components.note: American Quaker delegation's firsthand account of Emancipation Day in Anguilla.

components.title: Les colonies anglaises de 1574 à 1660
components.note: Names Anguilla in Charles I's 1627 Carlisle land grants. Translation ongoing.

components.title: Sailing Directions for the West Indies
components.note: Official nautical directions. Anguilla's coastline, reefs, and the 'Eel' etymology confirmed.

components.title: Modern Geography, Vol. 2
components.note: Anguillian settlers credited with founding the Virgin Islands colony. 911-page world gazetteer.

megabooks.title: Caribbean Cartography — 17th to 19th Century
megabooks.author: Various
megabooks.description: Historical nautical charts, Dutch Golden Age maps, and colonial survey maps of the Caribbean — all featuring Anguilla and the Lesser Antilles.

components.title: Pascaerte van de Caribes Eylanden (1675)
components.note: Dutch nautical chart of the Lesser Antilles by a celebrated Dutch ship's pilot.

components.title: Insulae Americanae in Oceano Septentrionali (1634)
components.note: Dutch Golden Age masterpiece. Amsterdam's Blaeu dynasty at its peak.

components.title: A Chart of the Caribe Ilands (1680)
components.note: Official hydrographer to the East India Company and Hudson's Bay Company.

components.title: Isole Antili, la Cuba e la Spagnuola (1690)
components.note: Venetian cosmographer who built globes for Louis XIV.

components.title: Tabula Mexicae et Floridae (1710)
components.note: Amsterdam's Schenk publishing house.

components.title: Carte Réduite des Antilles (1758)
components.note: French hydrographer royal — the authoritative French cartographic view of the Antilles.

components.title: Antillas Menores (1781)
components.note: Spanish royal cartographer's view of the Lesser Antilles.
